{"stdout":"# Architecture: Notes API

## Overview
One Node.js 24 process using the built-in `node:http` module. TypeScript files run
directly through type stripping (no build step, no npm dependencies).

```
src/
  server.ts   createServer(store, log) -> http.Server; routing + JSON I/O + request logging
  store.ts    NoteStore: in-memory Map<id, Note> (insertion-ordered)
  main.ts     entrypoint: reads PORT (default 8080), starts server, handles SIGTERM
scripts/
  smoke.ts    end-to-end checks against BASE_URL (default http://localhost:8080)
tests/        node:test suites (store, routes, logging, latency)
Dockerfile    node:24-alpine, CMD ["node", "src/main.ts"]
docker-compose.yml  service "notes", ports "8080:8080", healthcheck on /health
```

Layers follow SRP: `store.ts` has no HTTP knowledge; `server.ts` takes its store and
logger as arguments, so tests can run it on an ephemeral port and capture log lines.
IDs come from `crypto.randomUUID()` (built-in).

## Decisions

### ADR-001: Dependency-free in-memory service on node:http

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:** The PRD requires Node.js >= 24, TypeScript run directly by node, no npm dependencies, sub-50 ms p95 latency for up to 1,000 notes, and state held only in memory. Frameworks (Express, Fastify) and databases are ruled out by the no-dependency rule. Type stripping only supports erasable TypeScript syntax.
- **Decision:** Use `node:http` with a small hand-written router (method + path match, `/notes/:id` via a split on `/`). Keep notes in a `Map<string, Note>` inside a `NoteStore` class, with `crypto.randomUUID()` ids. Use only erasable TS syntax (no enums, namespaces or parameter properties) and `.ts` import specifiers. Log one line per request from the response `finish` event, using only method, path, status and duration. The body is never passed to the logger. Package as a `node:24-alpine` image run by docker compose on host port 8080.
- **Consequences:** No build step, nothing in the supply chain, and O(1) lookups keep latency well under budget. Notes are lost on restart (documented in README, an accepted non-goal). The hand-written router has to be tested explicitly for 404/400 paths. Type-stripping limits which TS features can be used.

### ADR-002: Smoke script as a standalone TypeScript program

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:** Deployment is checked by `npm run smoke` against the running container. It must exit non-zero on any failure and must not need any dependencies.
- **Decision:** `scripts/smoke.ts` uses global `fetch`, runs its checks in sequence (health, create, fetch-by-id), sets `process.exitCode = 1` and prints to stderr on the first failure. Each request has a timeout via `AbortSignal.timeout`.
- **Consequences:** The same script works locally and in CI against any `BASE_URL`. It checks only the happy path. Error-path behaviour is covered by `npm test`.

## NFR mapping

| NFR | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| NFR-1 | Every endpoint answers in under 50 ms p95 with 1,000 notes. Notes live in a `Map` with O(1) get/insert, list is a single pass over 1,000 entries, and there is no I/O beyond the socket. Checked by the latency test (AC-10). |
| NFR-2 | State is in memory only: one `NoteStore` instance per process, no disk or database. A restart clears notes, and the README says so. |
| NFR-3 | One log line per request is written on `res.on('finish')` with method, path, status and ms only. The logger never sees the body. Checked by the logging test with a unique marker (AC-9). |

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/cwijayasundaragmail.com/Documents/learning_101/run-greenfield3/docs/design/architecture.md","content":"# Architecture: Notes API

## Overview
One Node.js 24 process using the built-in `node:http` module. TypeScript files run
directly through type stripping (no build step, no npm dependencies).

```
src/
  server.ts   createServer(store, log) -> http.Server; routing + JSON I/O + request logging
  store.ts    NoteStore: in-memory Map<id, Note> (insertion-ordered)
  main.ts     entrypoint: reads PORT (default 8080), starts server, handles SIGTERM
scripts/
  smoke.ts    end-to-end checks against BASE_URL (default http://localhost:8080)
tests/        node:test suites (store, routes, logging, latency)
Dockerfile    node:24-alpine, CMD ["node", "src/main.ts"]
docker-compose.yml  service "notes", ports "8080:8080", healthcheck on /health
```

Layers follow SRP: `store.ts` has no HTTP knowledge; `server.ts` takes its store and
logger as arguments, so tests can run it on an ephemeral port and capture log lines.
IDs come from `crypto.randomUUID()` (built-in).

## Decisions

### ADR-001: Dependency-free in-memory service on node:http

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:** The PRD requires Node.js >= 24, TypeScript run directly by node, no npm dependencies, sub-50 ms p95 latency for up to 1,000 notes, and state held only in memory. Frameworks (Express, Fastify) and databases are ruled out by the no-dependency rule. Type stripping only supports erasable TypeScript syntax.
- **Decision:** Use `node:http` with a small hand-written router (method + path match, `/notes/:id` via a split on `/`). Keep notes in a `Map<string, Note>` inside a `NoteStore` class, with `crypto.randomUUID()` ids. Use only erasable TS syntax (no enums, namespaces or parameter properties) and `.ts` import specifiers. Log one line per request from the response `finish` event, using only method, path, status and duration. The body is never passed to the logger. Package as a `node:24-alpine` image run by docker compose on host port 8080.
- **Consequences:** No build step, nothing in the supply chain, and O(1) lookups keep latency well under budget. Notes are lost on restart (documented in README, an accepted non-goal). The hand-written router has to be tested explicitly for 404/400 paths. Type-stripping limits which TS features can be used.

### ADR-002: Smoke script as a standalone TypeScript program

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:** Deployment is checked by `npm run smoke` against the running container. It must exit non-zero on any failure and must not need any dependencies.
- **Decision:** `scripts/smoke.ts` uses global `fetch`, runs its checks in sequence (health, create, fetch-by-id), sets `process.exitCode = 1` and prints to stderr on the first failure. Each request has a timeout via `AbortSignal.timeout`.
- **Consequences:** The same script works locally and in CI against any `BASE_URL`. It checks only the happy path. Error-path behaviour is covered by `npm test`.

## NFR mapping

| NFR | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| NFR-1 | Every endpoint answers in under 50 ms p95 with 1,000 notes. Notes live in a `Map` with O(1) get/insert, list is a single pass over 1,000 entries, and there is no I/O beyond the socket. Checked by the latency test (AC-10). |
| NFR-2 | State is in memory only: one `NoteStore` instance per process, no disk or database. A restart clears notes, and the README says so. |
| NFR-3 | One log line per request is written on `res.on('finish')` with method, path, status and ms only. The logger never sees the body. Checked by the logging test with a unique marker (AC-9). |

Build a small HTTP service for personal notes.

## Requirements
- `POST /notes` with JSON {title, body} creates a note and returns 201 and the note with an id; an empty title returns 400.
- `GET /notes` lists notes; `GET /notes/:id` returns one note or 404.
- `GET /health` returns 200 {"status":"ok"}.

## Non-functional requirements
- Every endpoint responds in under 50 ms on a local machine (p95) for up to 1,000 stored notes.
- State is in memory; restarting the service clears notes (documented).
- The service logs one line per request and never logs request bodies.
